page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: What the cycle is
steps.why: The lining is rebuilt each month for a possible pregnancy, and shed when there is none, which is what makes it a cycle.
common_mistakes: Calling it the oestrous cycle. That is in other mammals.
Leaving out the length of the cycle.
steps.memory_tip: One ovum, one lining built and shed, about every 28 days.
steps.margin_note: Definition with the length, then the hormones.
lines: The menstrual cycle is the reproductive
cycle of human and other primate females.
One ovum is released in the middle of each
cycle. The endometrium of the uterus builds

steps.label: The four hormones
steps.why: Two hormones from the pituitary drive the ovary, and two from the ovary act back on the uterus.
common_mistakes: Naming only FSH and LH. Oestrogen and progesterone are also asked.
Giving the wrong source for each pair.
steps.memory_tip: FSH and LH from the pituitary; oestrogen and progesterone from the ovary.
steps.margin_note: Name the source beside each pair.
lines: The cycle is regulated by four hormones:
FSH and LH from the pituitary,

lines.text: and oestrogen and progesterone from the ovary

insider_note: Four hormones are asked for, from two glands. Group them: FSH and LH from the pituitary, oestrogen and progesterone from the ovary.
